title: Introduction & Writing the Attestation Record
text: I'm Uday Sanawane, and this is my week on Mycroft. I wrote the paperwork that says what I tested, then I did not promote the thing it documents, and that refusal is the week's actual work. Last episode, I gave two gates real failure paths. This week, I wrote the attestation, 125 lines recording what I actually ran, and then the recipe's own life cycle told me I could not mark it verified. One of the gates I had just fixed was the reason. Three questions decide whether a status is a fact or just a claim. One, what did you run named rows, not a feeling? That class already cost 782 purged rows. Question three, gate five was break tested four ways. No live call and no record passes. No live call with a recorded denial passes. A live call with an approval passes. And a live call against a recorded denial must fail. That is the only case that proves the gate reads the decision instead of just counting that one exists. So, here's what question three costs. The life cycle runs draft, specified, runnable sample, runnable live, verified. The recipe sits at runnable sample. title: The "Did Not Test" Log: Live Calls & Row Purges
text: Happened in a clearance that was refused. The falsifiable part, nine things broke while I was testing and had to be fixed and two of them were the gates from last episode. Gate five got fixed twice. First it passed if you did nothing, then it passed on the mere existence of a decision record, so the denial cleared it exactly as an approval would, which means last week's episode shipped a gate I had already called fixed. The attestation is evidence the testing was real. It is not evidence the thing works. Scored, what did I run? 17 rows, seven of them adversarial. What did I not run? 10 entries written down. Did a gate say no? Yes, and the status did not move. What verified would take is already written out in order. title: Gate 5 Denial & Refusing to Mark "Verified"
text: Judgement and it has already been made once and it was no. Your turn, find something in your project that carries a status verified, passing, production ready. Then ask what evidence would have to exist for that word to be true and whether anything ever said no. If the answer is that nobody checked, the word is a claim. The status is a claim.
